problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x-3y+2z=-4 \\ -4x+4y-3z=7 \\ x-y+z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-3y-2z=-2 \\ 5x+y+z=-1 \\ -8x+2y+z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ -13 & -15 & -11 \\ 18 & 22 & 16\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -2 \\ 5 & 1 & 1 \\ -8 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ -13 & -15 & -11 \\ 18 & 22 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=0,y=4,z=-5.$

Finally, $x+y+z=0+4+(-5)=-1.$
